phases.name: self-compact-worker
phases.description: T2 self-compact live round: one deepseek-v4-flash worker (1M-token window) whose pi argv carries the vendored self-compact extension (-e + 30%/50%/10% thresholds via the roster's harness_engineering/compaction fields), driven across the notice and warning thresholds until it writes a note_to_self, compacts, and receives the note back verbatim.
phases.task: You are a context-compaction test worker inside a software repository. Work strictly alone, never ask questions, and do not create or modify any repository files (writing scratch files under /tmp is allowed and required). A self-compact extension watches your context window and sends you [self-compact · ...] messages; you cannot see your usage otherwise. Goal: grow your own context usage in controlled steps until the warning threshold engages, compact, and then report. Procedure, one step per turn: 0. With the bash tool run exactly: for i in $(seq 1 20); do cat pi-vs-claude-code-vendor/coms-net.ts; done > /tmp/sc-fill.txt — then run: ls -l /tmp/sc-fill.txt — then call view_context (no arguments) once and remember used_percent and level as your baseline. 1. Read byte slice 1 of the fill file with bash: tail -c +1 /tmp/sc-fill.txt | head -c 600000. 2. Call view_context and remember the new level. 3. Continue with the next 600000-byte slice, one slice per turn (slice n: tail -c +N /tmp/sc-fill.txt | head -c 600000, with N = 600000 times (n-1) plus 1), a view_context after each, until view_context reports level at least "warning" or a [self-compact · WARNING] (or stronger) message appears. Do not stop before that. 4. The moment you are at warning or stronger: stop reading, write a concise note_to_self (goal; slices read so far; key observations; exact NEXT ACTION last: report the summary) and call self_compact as your ONLY tool call in that batch. 5. If every tool except self_compact is blocked, write the note and call self_compact immediately. 6. After your note_to_self is returned to you verbatim, read nothing more; finish with the required JSON reply whose result.summary states the highest self-compact level you observed (notice, warning or forced), that compaction ran, and the highest used_percent you saw.

phases.name: self-compact-close
phases.description: T2 self-compact closing sanity phase that exits cleanly; the schema wants at least two phases and this one is free.
